Recovery paths

`VaultWithdraw` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` call `canTransfer` between two pseudo-accounts (neither of which is the asset issuer), so the existing issuer carveout did not apply and withdrawals would fail with `tecNO_AUTH` after the issuer cleared `lsfMPTCanTransfer`.

A new `WaiveMPTCanTransfer` enum is threaded through `canTransfer`'s MPT and `Asset` overloads (default `No`, preserving every other call site). `VaultWithdraw` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` pass `Yes`, gated on the amendment.
Other transferability checks (IOU NoRipple, freeze, requireAuth) still apply.\r\n\r\n#### 2.

Vault share inheritance via `sfReferenceHolding`\r\n\r\nA new optional `UINT256` field on `MPTokenIssuance` points to the vault pseudo-account's holding for the underlying: the `MPToken` keylet for an MPT-backed vault, or the `RippleState` keylet for an IOU-backed vault.

XRP-backed vaults leave the field unset.

- `VaultCreate` populates the field at share-issuance creation. `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` validates the pointed-to SLE exists and is of an expected type (`ltMPTOKEN` or `ltRIPPLE_STATE`).
- `canTransfer(MPTIssue, ...)`, `canTrade(Asset)`, `isVaultPseudoAccountFrozen`, and `checkMPTAllowed` (AMM / Offer-crossing / Check) read `sfReferenceHolding`, fetch the holding SLE via `keylet::unchecked`, derive the underlying via a new `assetOfHolding` helper, and dispatch the same check recursively.
- Recursion is bounded at `kMAX_ASSET_CHECK_DEPTH` (vault-of-vault-shares is already forbidden at `VaultCreate`; the cap is defensive).

The bound and bookkeeping live inside the amendment-gated branch and are dead code pre-amendment.\r\n- The recovery-path waive short-circuits inheritance: callers operate on the vault's direct underlying, never on a share, so skipping the branch honors the recovery intent without transitively unlocking a deeper underlying.
The recursive call always passes `WaiveMPTCanTransfer::No`.\r\n\r\n#### 3.

Invariant

`ValidMPTIssuance` enforces, post-`fixCleanup3_2_0`:

- `sfReferenceHolding` may only be set on creation, only by `VaultCreate`.
- `sfReferenceHolding` is immutable on an existing `MPTokenIssuance`.
- Any `MPToken` / `RippleState` whose owner is a vault pseudo-account (account SLE has `sfVaultID`) may only be deleted by `VaultDelete`.

`visitEntry` bookkeeping is itself amendment-gated via the thread-local `isFeatureEnabled(fixCleanup3_2_0)` so pre-amendment transactions skip the new work entirely.

### API Impact

- [x] `libxrpl` change — new `sfReferenceHolding` field on `MPTokenIssuance`; new `WaiveMPTCanTransfer` enum; new `assetOfHolding` helper.

No public API or peer-protocol changes.

All behavior gated under `fixCleanup3_2_0`.

## Test Plan

Covered in `Vault_test`, `Loan_test`, and `Invariants_test`:

- `sfReferenceHolding` writer correctness — populated by `VaultCreate` for MPT/IOU underlyings, unset for XRP, absent pre-amendment, absent for plain `MPTokenIssuanceCreate`.
- Recovery paths — post-amendment `VaultWithdraw` / `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` succeed after issuer clears `lsfMPTCanTransfer`; pre-amendment regression confirms historical failure mode.
- Share inheritance — P2P share Payment and IOU `NoRipple` propagation through `canTransfer`; DEX offers blocked through `canTrade`; AMM creation with shares blocked through `checkMPTAllowed` when the underlying `CanTrade` is cleared.

No (or insufficient) re-validation of pending/in-flight confidential proofs or version counters occurs on mutable field changes.

The current commit's implementation of sfMutableFlags + confidential hooks leaves a TOCTOU-style window.

High severity due to core accounting soundness risk.

Proof of Concept (Coded skeleton — executable via public JSON-RPC on local contest node once amendments enabled): Setup (run first): Issuer submits MPTokenIssuanceCreate with mutable MaxAmount (set sfMutableFlags appropriately per XLS-94).

Attack Sequence: Perform several ConfidentialMPTSend / Convert txs (ZK proofs validated against original MaxAmount).

### Context of Change

In #5224 we added `DomainID` as an access control mechanism for `SingleAssetVault`.

The actual implementation of this feature lies in `MPToken` and `MPTokenIssuance`, hence it makes sense to enable the use of `DomainID` also in `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceSet`, following same rules as in Vault:

* `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceSet` can only set `DomainID` if flag `MPTRequireAuth` is set
* `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` requires that `DomainID` be a non-zero, uint256 number
* `MPTokenIssuanceSet` allows `DomainID` to be zero (or empty) in which case it will remove `DomainID` from the `MPTokenIssuance` object

The change is amendment-gated by `SingleAssetVault`.
